mission_07: Streaming Automatic Speech Recognition processes audio in real-time as it arrives, producing partial transcriptions with low latency rather than waiting for the complete utterance. This is essential for live captioning, voice assistants, and real-time translation. The key challenge is maintaining recognition accuracy while processing incomplete audio, which requires careful management of encoder state across chunks and handling of word boundaries that may span chunk boundaries. Chunked processing divides the audio stream into fixed-size segments with overlap to preserve context at boundaries. The encoder maintains a hidden state that is passed from one chunk to the next, allowing the model to build on previously computed representations. Feature extraction is performed on each chunk independently, typically computing log-power spectra or filter bank features. The decoder produces token predictions for each chunk, which are accumulated into a running transcript. The finalize method processes any remaining audio in the buffer after the stream ends. In this mission, you will implement a complete streaming ASR system with chunked processing, stateful encoding, greedy decoding, and buffer management.
